cards.title: Mixing (Strong Mixing)
cards.body: Let (X,Sigma,mu) be a probability space and T: X -> X measure-preserving. T is (strongly) mixing if mu(T^{-n}A cap B) -> mu(A)mu(B) as n -> infinity for all measurable A, B in Sigma, so that the sets T^{-n}A become asymptotically independent of B in the measure-theoretic sense. Strong mixing implies weak mixing (the Cesaro-averaged statement (1/N) sum_{n=0}^{N-1} |mu(T^{-n}A cap B) - mu(A)mu(B)| -> 0), and weak mixing implies ergodicity; neither implication reverses in general.

cards.title: Attempt on Existence of a hexatic phase for two-dimensional Riesz gases
cards.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Source-specific calculation, conditional implication or exact obstruction Result: A rotationally invariant Gibbs mixture can have zero mean orientational order while retaining long-range two-point order. As a diagnostic let theta_x=Theta+eta_x, where Theta is uniform modulo2*pi and the eta_x are iid. Then E exp(6*i*theta_x)=0, but for x distinct from y, E exp(6*i*(theta_x-theta_y))=|E exp(6*i*eta_x)|^2, which can be strictly positive. Check: The global angle cancels in the difference and independence factors the two local terms into conjugates. Taking all eta_x=0 gives two-point order1 despite the zero one-point mean. Obstruction: Consequently a vanishing rotation-averaged one-point order parameter cannot rule out the proposed phase. A proof must establish the proper bond-orientational correlations together with positional decorrelation for the actual Gibbs law, with defects and thermodynamic limits controlled.

cards.title: Open problem: Existence of a hexatic phase for two-dimensional Riesz gases
cards.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status unsolved). Prove or refute the intermediate hexatic phase predicted in two-dimensional Riesz-gas phase diagrams, distinguished by orientational order and absence of crystalline positional order. Source: Lewin: Coulomb and Riesz gases, the known and the unknown,2022, SectionVI.B,PDF66-67.
